author: SureshKBN
text:
Nureca
Look at the sales and EBIDTA margin trend; it is not a fluke; it came from a structural change in business.

What they did
-Set up in-house manufacturing via subsidiary
-Focused only on:
     High-volume
     Margin-sensitive
     Regulated products
-From Flipkart/amazon to Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart, D2C and offline expansion.

Structural levers still ahead

-Manufacturing share moving from ~32% → 45–50%
-Punjab plant commissioning → scale economics
-Exports (US FDA approval already in place)
-Offline + quick commerce still under-penetrated
-Optional monetisation of Dr Trust 360 ecosystem

Biggest risk -
Keep an eye on trade receivable and OCF.

It's not a buy or sell recommendation, just for information only,

author: SureshKBN
text:
During the transformer explosive price action  2–3 years ago, many low-float transformer stocks grabbed all the attention. They moved wildly, looked irresistible, and created the illusion of easy money. Yet very few investors made meaningful gains, and many found themselves trapped when liquidity vanished.

Be careful with low-float stocks being marketed as AI proxies today. Read the business, understand the balance sheet, study execution, and assess management quality.

Tailwinds can lift a good business higher, but no tailwind can permanently save a poorly run business

author: SureshKBN
text:

author: SureshKBN
text:
I like the efforts u put in and can not ignore this questions. but if you carefully observe my post on PEAD I already answered these .let me add further details.

1. Creating a Watchlist

Focus on Strong Sectors: Pay attention to companies in fast-growing areas like power, renewables, data centers, AI, and recycling.
Stay Prepared: Update your watchlist before companies announce their results so you're ready to act quickly if needed.

2. Dealing with Unknown Companies

Look for Strong Performers: Check for companies that are close to their 52-week high, which might mean they’re doing well. . I got Tembo like this .
Use Tools and Social Media: Websites like  can help you filter companies by performance, and Twitter can give you quick updates on results.

3. What to Look For in a Company

Financial Health: Look at revenue growth (how much the company is earning), profit growth, improving profit margins, and future plans, often found in investor presentations.
See how Amy organics got rerate after growth guidance increased further .
 Tembo leadership released first PPT with strong growth guidance and restructuring into power and defense .
You also need to learn on valuations . You can learn this in YouTube and see SOIC free videos r course .
Join Earnings Calls: Listening to these calls can help you understand the company’s spending plans and growth goals, and clear up any doubts.

4. Learning Takes Time don't be in hurray FOMO -

No Fixed Formula: Don’t rely too much on strict rules or formulas. Investing is simple and yet complex at the same time , and some things only make sense after you’ve gained some experience.
Keep Trying: The more you practice, the more you’ll learn. Some lessons can’t be explained easily; you just have to keep at it.

contextText:
Standard Glass Lining has been talking about how glass-lined shell & tube (S&T) heat exchangers could be a game changer for their company 🚀

Even industry leaders like GMM Pfaudler and HLE Glascoat don’t have this tech - only one Japanese company 🇯🇵 in the world has mastered it.

But… what’s so special about this thing? Why is it such a big deal for pharma? Lets try to understand it 👇

1️⃣ First, what are S&T heat exchangers?
A shell & tube heat exchanger is basically a bundle of metal tubes inside a metal “shell.” One fluid flows through the tubes, another flows outside them in the shell - heat passes through the tube walls, and both fluids stay separate .

They’re used everywhere - chemicals ⚗️, power plants ⚡, pharma 💊 - because they handle large heat loads efficiently.

2️⃣ Why does pharma care?
In pharma manufacturing, many steps involve heating or cooling corrosive fluids - acids, solvents, brines. You need a heat exchanger material that:
- Resists corrosion
- Doesn’t contaminate the product
- Is easy to clean & validate under GMP rules

3️⃣ What is pharma mostly using today?
For highly corrosive duties, pharma often uses graphite block heat exchangers. Graphite is chemically resistant, so it doesn’t corrode easily, and it’s been the “go-to” for decades in this niche.

4️⃣ The problem with graphite
Over time, pharma discovered some serious GMP headaches:
- Particle shedding - Graphite is porous & brittle. Even with resin impregnation, tiny carbon particles can flake into the product.
- Adsorption: Graphite can absorb actives/impurities, leading to cross-batch contamination.
- Cleaning difficulty: Porous surfaces trap residues; cleaning takes longer and can still fail swab tests.
- Brittleness: Thermal shock or mechanical impact can crack blocks, leading to costly downtime.

In an API plant, these are not just inconveniences - they can cause entire batch rejections and inspection troubles.

5️⃣ Why glass-lined S&T is exciting
This new design uses a normal steel shell & tube exchanger, but every wetted surface - inside the tubes, the shell, the tube sheets - is coated with a smooth, inert borosilicate glass layer.
Benefits over graphite:
- No particle shedding
- No adsorption, nothing gets “stuck” in the surface
- Faster, easier cleaning & validation
- Steel underneath = stronger, less fragile
- Better heat transfer area per footprint

For pharma, that means cleaner batches, less downtime, better compliance, and potentially millions saved in reduced rejections and cleaning costs.

6️⃣ Why doesn’t everyone make this?
Glass-lining a reactor vessel is common - many companies do it. But glass-lining thin tubes and the tube-to-tube-sheet joints inside an S&T exchanger is incredibly difficult.
You need:
- Uniform glass coating inside long, narrow tubes without pinholes
- Special sealing methods at the tube sheets that survive thermal cycling without cracking the glass
- Firing and cooling processes that avoid stress fractures
- 100% defect-free production, because pharma won’t tolerate even one flake of glass

This takes decades of R&D and manufacturing discipline.

7️⃣ The monopoly
For years, only one Japanese company mastered this technology at scale for GMP use. They had the know-how, the QC systems, and the proven performance.

Recently, Standard Glass Lining signed an exclusive licence to assemble and market this Japanese design in India. That’s why they keep calling it a game changer - it’s a proven, monopoly-grade technology, now finally available locally.

💡 Bottom line
Pharma wants to move from graphite to glass-lined S&T because it solves contamination, cleaning, and reliability issues while keeping corrosion resistance.
The barrier was supply - and Standard’s deal with the Japanese supplier just broke that barrier.

Standard Glass estimates 2,000 crores of opportunity in this segment.
New facility comes live in Jan'26, where they would be able to manufacture 300 glass lined S&T per month.

contextText:
L&T Finance MD Sudipta Roy: "Weak Monsoon Poses Limited Risk on Portfolio," Targets 20%+ AUM Growth Under Lakshya 2031

AUM Growth Target for FY27
As part of the Lakshya 2031 plan, L&T Finance targets AUM growth of more than 20% and remains committed to that

Sudipta Roy, MD & CEO: "If there is risk-calibrated growth available in the market, we will not shy away from taking it. However, we are cautious because of the risk of an uneven monsoon and the ongoing West Asia conflict"

Company remains focused on its current portfolio mix — secured-to-unsecured mix is about 57:43, with a target to maintain at 60:40 over the next two years

Weak Monsoon's Impact on Microfinance
On how weak monsoon is influencing the outlook for the microfinance sector: "The microfinance industry has come out of an asset quality cycle. About 18 months after a stress, we hit a Goldilocks window with little risk emergence. The microfinance sector's balance sheets have contracted and industry is quite deleveraged. So, even a weaker monsoon — given healthy reservoir levels — shouldn't cause significant spillovers. I expect the industry to remain stable this fiscal year"

Cost of Funds & Margins — FY27 Outlook
On how cost of funds and margins are expected to pan out in FY27, given possible MCLR hike: "We expect NIM plus fee income to remain within the guided range of 10-10.5%. Therefore, I don't expect the weighted average borrowing cost to rise. It should stay stable or improve slightly"

Impact of New Gold Loan Rules (Introduced April)
New RBI circular requires bureau checks for loans of certain ticket sizes, which has hurt customers with poor credit histories

Industry has adopted tiered LTVs (loan-to-value ratios) based on ticket size and is still adjusting to the change

April volumes fell sharply, but they began normalising in May-June

Roy expects the industry to get back to normal trajectory in Q2

Core Theme:
Roy's interview reflects a company balancing ambitious growth targets with deliberate risk calibration — the commitment to 20%+ AUM growth under Lakshya 2031 is real, but explicitly conditional on "risk-calibrated" opportunities rather than growth for its own sake, echoing a broader theme seen across NBFC and bank commentary this cycle of prioritizing balance-sheet discipline over aggressive expansion. The most reassuring data point is the microfinance sector's post-stress deleveraging: having already worked through an 18-month asset quality cycle, the industry entering this monsoon season with contracted, lighter balance sheets means a weak monsoon is unlikely to trigger the kind of spillover stress it might have caused during the sector's more leveraged phase — while the new gold loan bureau-check rules represent a near-term, self-correcting disruption (sharp April volume drop, already normalising by June) rather than a structural headwind, suggesting Roy sees FY27 as a year of steady, controlled growth rather than one requiring defensive positioning.

author: SureshKBN
text:
Sales growth is the top.
But money has to flow down till EPS.

Sales up, but gross margin flat
Company is selling more, but not making better profit on each product. Pricing power is weak.

Gross margin up, but OPM flat
Product margin improved, but employee costs and other expenses ate the benefit.

OPM up, but PAT flat
Business profit improved, but interest cost, depreciation, tax, or one-offs took away the gain.

PAT up, but EPS flat
Company profit increased, but shareholders did not benefit much because of dilution.
So don’t get excited by sales growth alone.

Real growth is when sales growth converts into margin expansion, PAT growth and finally EPS growth.

Growth matters only when it reaches the shareholder.

text:
1. Vertical Turbine Pumps (VTPs):
Key Role: Used for lifting massive volumes of water across varying elevations, a critical need in river-linking projects.
Features:High-capacity water handling (up to tens of thousands of cubic meters per hour).
Designed to operate efficiently under high head and large discharge conditions.
Corrosion-resistant materials to handle sediment-laden river water.

2. Vertical Axial Flow Pumps:
Key Role: Ideal for transferring large quantities of water at low to medium heads, commonly used in river linking for low-lift areas.
Features:High efficiency in handling large flows.
Durable impellers and components for long-term operations.
Customizable for specific site conditions.

3. Horizontal Split Case Pumps:
Key Role: Used in pumping stations for high-pressure water transfer over long distances.
Features:Robust design for continuous operation.
Low maintenance requirements.
High energy efficiency to minimize operational costs.

4. Flood Control and Drainage Pumps:
Key Role: Deployed in river-linking projects to handle excess water during monsoons or manage water levels in interconnected basins.
Features:Large discharge capacity to prevent flooding.
Engineered for handling high sediment loads and debris.

5. Specialized Pumping Systems for Lift Irrigation:
Key Role: WPIL supplies integrated systems to lift water from lower basins to higher altitudes, essential in hilly terrains and inter-basin water transfer.
Features:Customized to meet the elevation and flow requirements of the specific project.
Equipped with energy-efficient motors and controls.

6. Turnkey Pumping Stations:
Key Role: WPIL constructs and supplies fully operational pumping stations, which serve as the backbone of river-linking infrastructure.
Features:Multiple pumps working in tandem to meet the high discharge and head requirements.
Complete with control systems, pipelines, and auxiliary equipment.
Designed for seamless integration with the overall water transfer system.

7. Automation and Control Systems:
Key Role: Integrated with pumping systems to ensure smooth operation and real-time monitoring in large-scale river-linking projects.
Features:Remote monitoring and diagnostics.
Advanced flow and pressure control for optimal performance.
Energy optimization features to reduce operational costs.

Examples of Use in River-Linking Projects:
Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Scheme (Telangana):Supplied vertical turbine and axial flow pumps for one of the world's largest lift irrigation projects.

Polavaram Project (Andhra Pradesh):Delivered pumps to lift and transfer water across basins.

Ken-Betwa River Linking Project (Proposed):WPIL is positioned to contribute similar high-capacity pumping solutions.

Why WPIL’s Products are Crucial for River-Linking:
Ability to handle high water volumes and variable head requirements.
Energy-efficient solutions to minimize costs in large-scale projects.
Customization for sediment-heavy river water and site-specific challenges.
These products and solutions enable WPIL to play a pivotal role in India’s river-linking initiatives by ensuring reliable, long-term water transfer systems.

author: SureshKBN
text:
When the growth rate starts to decelerate compared to valuations, as reflected in the PEG ratio, management often guides expectations accordingly. However, the PEG is subjective (so I am not giving any number intentionally) , depending on the company’s phase of growth.

I bought TRIL when it was priced at ₹160, despite it having a higher P/E than it does now.
The same scenario played out with Schneider, as well as with E2E and NPST.
There are many stocks since my beginning days.

Initially, I used to believe that quality never comes cheap. However, it's crucial to differentiate between genuine growth potential and market euphoria.

The most important aspect is how you interpret future growth by connecting multiple data points. You can't simply reduce this to a rigid framework or formula based on base, bull, or bear cases. While those are necessary, they aren't the whole story.

On a side note, it seems that Twitter has flagged some of your comments as spam.

author: SureshKBN
text:
**Understanding and Leveraging Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift (PEAD): My Approach**

**What is PEAD?**
Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift (PEAD) occurs when a company’s earnings report, commentary, or conference call introduces a significant surprise for the market—often positive—that isn’t fully reflected in the stock price immediately. The delayed reaction can be due to market participants underestimating the impact or needing more time to fully digest the news. This creates a potential opportunity, as the market’s gradual realization of this “surprise” can drive up the stock price over days, weeks, or even months. In my view, these PEAD scenarios offer compelling cases to buy, either because the stock becomes undervalued based on future growth potential or because it offers a short-term value play.

---

**How I Identify PEAD Opportunities:**

1. **Tracking Company Results Closely**
I keep a close eye on company earnings reports, commentary, and quarterly announcements. To do this, I use platforms like [Screener]() to review growth metrics, and I follow accounts like @nid_rockz on Twitter for additional insights. My focus includes:
- **Top-line and Bottom-line Growth**: Is there revenue (top-line) or profit (bottom-line) growth that exceeds expectations?
- **Margin Expansion**: Are the company’s profit margins improving significantly, hinting at higher operational efficiency or pricing power?
- **Guidance and Commentary**: Any forward-looking statements from management that suggest stronger performance or strategic shifts also catch my attention.

2. **Prioritizing Sectors with Strong Tailwinds**
Certain sectors have structural tailwinds that can amplify a PEAD effect, making them high-priority targets. I closely track companies in industries such as:
- **Power & Renewable Energy**: Given the global push for sustainable energy, companies here often have strong demand drivers.
- **Data Centers (DC)**: With the rise of cloud computing and digital transformation, this sector continues to see robust growth.
- **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**: Many tech companies leveraging AI innovations have high growth potential.
- **Recycling and Sustainability**: As ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) factors become increasingly important, recycling and sustainability-focused companies often receive favorable attention and growth opportunities.

3. **Utilizing Scanners to Catch Missed Opportunities**
If I overlook something in steps 1 or 2, I turn to stock scanners for additional insights. Specifically, I look for stocks reaching or approaching 52-week highs. When a stock is consistently moving upward, it could signal underlying growth that the market is recognizing. From there, I “reverse engineer” by:
- Reviewing recent earnings reports, management commentary, and earnings calls to see if the upward movement aligns with a PEAD pattern.
- Examining the company’s leadership track record to assess if they’ve consistently delivered on growth projections or successfully navigated challenges.

---

**Avoiding Rigid Formulas**
While these steps guide my process, I consciously avoid locking myself into a strict formula or framework. PEAD opportunities are as much about understanding market sentiment as they are about crunching numbers. Flexibility in assessing each situation is key.

---

**My Buy and Sell Strategy**

**When I Buy**
I only buy stocks **after** the earnings release, not before. Acting on earnings results requires agility, as it’s essential to quickly interpret both the company’s historical performance and the implications of the latest results. This agility allows me to respond effectively to the PEAD effect as it starts to unfold.

**When I Sell**
For **non-structural, short-term opportunities**, I generally sell once the valuation gap has been filled—when the market has fully priced in the positive earnings surprise. However, for **core, long-term positions**, I stay invested as long as the company continues to show promise. I hold these positions until I see a better opportunity elsewhere or if there’s a substantial change in the company's outlook.

---

author: SureshKBN
text:
Themes matter.

If one studies stocks that did best in any given year, the big moves always have a big thematic tailwind behind them.

Once a theme is identified by the market - a big re rating is likely over the next 1 to 3 years.

How to identify a theme?

News - typically an event triggers a theme. This event is typically reported in the news. It could be regulatory or a new category growing fast.

Corporate announcements- more relevant for individual stocks to take off. But development in one stock can give clues about entire sector.

52 week high lists - These dont help you get in first but still can provide clues to where the action is happening. The key here is to look for recent 52 week highs and not the ones which have been going up for more than one or two years - where you are likely already late, but not always.

These lists have to be gone through with the context of looking for emerging themes.

Once a theme is identified typically all stocks in that sector are rerated irrespective of current earnings. The valuations may or may not make sense today but market is ALWAYS looking at future.

The current fate of PGIL/SPAL is tied to just two triggers  USA tariff resolution and the UK FTA getting legal status.

USA tariffs are the real key. If they’re not resolved by December, many customers will shift sourcing to other countries. Once they move out, getting them back is a slow, painful cycle.

For now, companies are surviving by sharing the burden with clients, cutting capacity, or diverting orders to other geographies.

UK FTA legal status by March can act as fuel on fire for exports.

If both go through, I easily see 50% upside in 12–18 months.
If they don’t, the burden continues with slow, grinding growth.

Key Triggers for Recent Gains in HEG and Graphite India

1. Capacity Expansion at HEG
HEG has completed expanding its graphite electrode plant to 100,000 tonnes, making it the largest single-location plant in the western world.
This gives HEG a competitive edge with cost advantages and scalability, especially as it maintains a world-leading 80% capacity utilization rate.

2. China's Export Restrictions
China has tightened its review of graphite exports to the US and banned certain graphite-related commodities like Germanium and Gallium.
These measures, part of China's response to US semiconductor restrictions, have caused supply concerns globally, benefiting Indian graphite electrode makers.

3. PLI Scheme for Electric Battery Components
Reports suggest the Indian government is considering a Rs. 9,000 crore Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for electric battery component manufacturing.
This is expected to boost demand for graphite products, contributing to investor interest in HEG and Graphite India.

4. Demand from Decarbonization
Global decarbonization efforts are driving a shift toward Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) steelmaking, which uses graphite electrodes.
More than 100 million tonnes of new EAF capacity are expected to be operational by 2030, creating a long-term demand boost.

Market Response
HEG shares surged 17% and Graphite India shares rose 10%, marking their highest gains in weeks.
Both companies featured in Jefferies' top stock picks, adding to the positive momentum.

Long-Term Prospects
HEG and Graphite India rely heavily on exports, with HEG exporting about two-thirds of its production for over 30 years.
India’s rising steel demand (projected to grow 8% in 2024-25) further strengthens their outlook.

Challenges and Competitors
HEG faces global demand pressure, reducing pricing power in the short term. However, subsidies could significantly improve project returns (payback period reduced from 9-10 years to 6 years).
Major global competitors like GrafTech International and Resonac (Showa Denko) have double the capacity of Indian players, but HEG remains optimistic about its export-led growth.

contextText:
How a rookie mistake of mine converted a would-be 25R trade into a minus 1R trade. 🙈

This morning at around 9:20am, I was interested in buying #ECOSMOBLTY and had a lot of conviction in this trade. I placed a buy order at 506 and a sell order at 503. Since I am busy and don't have much time, I quickly placed the orders and then continued with my desk job.

Usually, when you do not hold a stock and the sell order triggers first, it gets rejected because you do not have that holding. Even if it triggers first, it's no problem. Then if the buy order gets triggered, and that's okay. I placed both orders because I anticipated a busy day and wouldn't have got time to place a sell order later, & the SL was too tight at only ₹3.

What happened was that I was unaware that I was placing MIS intraday orders. 🤦🏻‍♂️

For a moment, the price went below 503, and the sell order triggered first, leaving me short on this stock. Then the price moved up, and now the buy order served as the stoploss order. I was out of this trade with -1R, while the price continued to make highs.

But I didn't know this till I got the time to look at the TradingView window at around 11:30am (tea break). I saw it had moved about 5-6% up from my buy price. But when I checked my broker's account, to my dismay, I was out of this trade with a -1R.

Even after so many years of trading, I'm still making rookie mistakes. When will I learn? 🤪

I see many tagging me whenever textile companies report good results.

But we need to separate what is driving the improvement new capex going live, a better product mix, inventory gains, or genuine export demand.

The bigger triggers are the UK FTA, the US 10% tariff advantage, and the upcoming EU FTA expected in H2 FY27. These can expand the addressable market for Indian textile companies in one go.

But this cannot be understood from headline numbers alone. You need to read the investor presentation and listen to the earnings call to know which companies are actually positioned to benefit, how large the opportunity is, and when it can reflect in revenues.

If you find any company management giving clear insights or numbers around these triggers, tag me.

contextText:
Venus Pipes has seen a turnaround in domestic business in last 2 quarters and now tariffs getting reduced, the exports here might also fire. Tracking not invested. Concall notes -

1. Domestic Order Execution & Guidance
Question (Parth Bhavsar - Investec): Regarding the INR 190 crore order won in April/February, what is the status of execution? Is the guidance for FY26 maintained?
Management Response (Kunal Bubna):Execution Status: More than 15% of the order has been executed. The balance is currently under execution.
Timeline: The internal target is to finish this order before June 2026.
Guidance: The company maintains its revenue growth guidance of 25% for FY26.

2. Margins (EBITDA) & Future Outlook
Question (Dhruv Jain - Ambit Capital): With new capacities and value addition coming online, how should we look at margins in FY27? Why aren't margins jumping higher than the 16-18% range despite fittings and value addition?
Management Response (Kunal Bubna):Current Margin: Margins for Q3 FY26 stood at 16.3%.
FY27 Outlook: Margins are expected to be in the 16% to 18% range on a blended basis.
Reasoning: While value-added capacities (welded, seamless, fittings) will come online by the end of this financial year, the fittings business is new. It requires customer approvals, which take time. Therefore, while margins will be higher than current levels, the 16-18% range is the realistic target for the near term,.

Question (Mythili Balakrishnan - Alchemy): If steel prices stay on an upward trajectory, what happens to margins given the company is short cycle?
Management Response (Kunal Bubna): The company generally tries to hedge raw material prices while taking orders. Therefore, margins are not significantly affected by price fluctuations.
Question (Pallav Agarwal - Antique Stock Broking): Why have margins remained stagnant at ~16-16.5% despite the understanding that seamless pipes (backward integrated) have better margins?
Management Response (Kunal Bubna): Margins have remained constant, but volume and value have increased despite subdued demand in some markets. The "bump up" in margins is expected in the coming year as new capacities start operating at optimum levels.
3. Export Market Dynamics (US, Europe, Middle East)
Question (Dhruv Jain - Ambit Capital & Sneha Talreja - Nuvama): How will the domestic vs. export mix change in the second half? What is the impact of tariffs on US exports?

Management Response (Kunal Bubna):Export Mix: Exports contributed ~40% in Q2, but due to US uncertainty (tariffs), this might normalize to 25-30% going forward. The rest of the growth will be domestic-driven.
Geography: Good orders are coming from Europe. The US market is seeing a slight decline due to uncertainty. The Middle East remains stable.
US Share: US exports constituted around 20% of total exports in Q2.

Question (Bhargav - Ambit Asset Management): Are tariffs passed on to customers in the US?

Management Response (Kunal Bubna): Yes. For current orders, the understanding is that tariffs are passed on to the end customer. The company is currently tariff-neutral.
Question (Ritesh Shah - Investec): What is the effective tariff against Europe and the US? How does CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) affect the outlook?

Management Response (Kunal Bubna):Europe: No specific tariff on India currently, whereas China faces substantial tariffs.
US: Section 232 tariff is 25% (transcript notes 50%, likely referring to combined duties on competitors or specific anti-dumping scenarios, but clarifies India is cheaper compared to China).
CBAM: Europe has not yet standardized values for seamless pipes. Venus is evaluating this and believes they are near the standard based on consultant discussions.

4. Order Book & Sectoral Demand
Question (Dhruv Jain - Ambit Capital): What is the current order book size?
Management Response (Kunal Bubna): The order book stands at INR 490 crores.
Question (Bhargav - Ambit Asset Management): Regarding the BHEL/Power sector, tenders worth INR 3,000-4,000 crores are expected. What is your thought on this?
Management Response (Kunal Bubna & Arun Kothari):Capex in the thermal sector is significantly high.
Status: Venus has already participated in several tenders. Management anticipates 80% of large tenders will open in the next 3 to 4 months (H2 FY26 or early April),.
Competition: There are typically 5-7 buyers/bidders competing for these contracts.

5. Fittings & New Capacities
Question (Sneha Talreja - Nuvama & Bhargav - Ambit): What is the revenue contribution expected from fittings in FY26? What is the peak revenue potential?

Management Response (Kunal Bubna):FY26 Contribution: Not much revenue is expected from the new fittings plant in FY26 as it starts in the last quarter (Q4).
Peak Potential: The asset turnover is expected to be 3x the investment. With a capex of ~INR 60 crores for fittings, peak revenue could be INR 180-200 crores,.
Ramp-up: Fittings is a new business requiring approvals, so it will take time to ramp up compared to seamless pipes where the company is already established.

6. Operational Costs & Balance Sheet
Question (Pallav Agarwal - Antique Stock Broking): Employee costs and other expenses have gone up. Will this stabilize?
Management Response (Kunal Bubna): Costs are increasing because new plants/expansions are starting each quarter. These costs should stabilize after this year once operations normalize.
Question (Pallav Agarwal - Antique Stock Broking): Borrowings have increased. Are we close to peak net debt?

Management Response (Kunal Bubna): Debt will increase slightly further as there is still remaining capex to be funded. A few more loans will come onto the books.
7. Anti-Dumping Duty (ADD)
Question (Pallav Agarwal - Antique Stock Broking): When do the anti-dumping duties on stainless steel pipes expire?

Management Response (Kunal Bubna): The ADD was implemented in December 2022 for 5 years, so it is expected to expire around December 2027.
8. Approvals & Strategy
Question (Ritesh Shah - Investec): Which specific approvals are you working on?
Management Response (Kunal Bubna & Arun Kothari): The company is working on approvals in the Middle East, Southeast Asia, USA, Brazil, and Europe. This is an ongoing process involving oil & gas companies. Specific names were kept confidential due to competition,.
Question (Ritesh Shah - Investec): Any plans for a captive furnace (backward integration into steel making)?

Management Response (Kunal Bubna): Currently, there are no plans for backward integration into the "round side" (steel making/furnace).

Below is all that matters. Everything else is just narrative, to whoever it suits best.

- DeepSeek is an incredible feat in the evolution of AI, the next big inflection point after ChatGPT released in Nov 2022.

- They have proved once again what we have known forever: in AI, talent over everything else. It was the very reason a non-profit lab called OpenAI was put together in 2015, to assimilate the best research talent to take on Google. DS has played the exact same move against OAI a decade later.

- The difference this time is that the talent is not what you would typically think AI Research, but rather a crack team of software engineers, infra architects, mathematicians and DevOps. This IMO is as significant a moment as anything else, that to build great AI models you no longer need to compete for limited expensive AI talent ($1-5m salaries).

- This would not have been possible without decades of AI research compounding, and without OpenAI o3 already being out there. DS used AI to generate data to build best in class AI. The hilarious part is OpenAI still makes a unit loss on their inference, which means DS caused them losses in more ways than one!

- Even if DS is fabricating the costs, the paper proves it is still an order of magnitude cheaper than anything else so far of similar quality. This will lead to an explosion of more teams & companies building models, and many will play in specific niches. This is a very very good thing.

- As a result, the eventual demand for compute will still stay in a similar range, or maybe even to up because so many players will now get into the game. Jevons Paradox in full action.

- Cheaper models will lead to cheaper inference. Cheaper inference will lead to startups using AI for all sorts of things for both building products and internal tools. Cost of company building will go down and the one person $1b enterprise that Sam has talked about is no longer a pipe dream.

- This also has implications on Venture Capital in AI. IMO there will be small funds and then very large funds. A $1m seed can now probably take you very far, even profitability. And then you need serious growth capital for world dominance. Good time to be in private equity.

What a time to be alive, and fortunate to be working in this industry. Time to put India on the map! 🚀🇮🇳

Q) Why did you start reducing power sector exposure?

Because price action told me the sector already ran ahead of its fundamentals. When stocks stop reacting to good results, the market is saying “the story is fully priced.”

Q) Has the power sector reached its peak in price action?

Not “peak fundamentals,” but peak enthusiasm.

Leaders across generation, transmission, distribution and EPC already had their big rerating. The easy money was made.

Q) Who are the leaders in the power sector today?

The top names in each vertical that already rerated heavily.
When the market selects its champions, outsized returns shrink for new investors.

Q) Why is the market not reacting despite good results?

Because the market expected these results.
When good numbers give flat or negative movement, it means valuation already captured the growth.

Q) Has valuation caught up with growth?

In many cases, yes.
Now earnings must work for 1–2 years just to justify today’s prices   not to give fresh returns.

Q) Are there better opportunities in other sectors?

Yes.
If capital can earn better risk–reward elsewhere  with reasonable valuations and undiscovered leaders —it makes sense to rotate.

This is not exiting in fear but it’s upgrading opportunity cost.

Q) Is the power story over?
No.
But the return profile has changed.
From “high returns, low expectations” to “steady returns, high expectations.”

contextText:
MOSL note:

FINANCIALS | BANKS: Ground zero: Channel check – Boots, branches, and beyond

We interacted with various direct loan selling agents (DSAs), covering the corporate and retail segments, to gain insights into the credit demand outlook and emerging asset quality trends. Following are the key takeaways:

# PSU banks have emerged as the dominant force in MSME lending, gaining market share over the past 6 to 9 months on the back of CGTMSE-backed lending, and repo-linked pricing. This has significantly narrowed the cost gap compared to private banks.

# Unsecured business lending is undergoing a reset, with growth moderating to ~10-20% from 30-40% in prior years. Despite a sharp correction in pricing (~12-12.5%), demand has not revived meaningfully.

# Collection intensity has increased in unsecured MSME, with higher recovery costs and more tactical borrower behavior.

# Housing and real estate momentum remains intact, led by a pickup in disbursements and strong activity among large developers.

# PSU banks have regained relevance in home loans, supported by lower pricing, improved turnaround times, and normalized DSA commissions (0.8–1.2%), aiding traction in Tier-2/3 cities.

# Credit card growth remains subdued, with issuances continuing to be selective. Early stress indicators are stabilizing, though delinquency levels remain elevated compared to historical norms.

author: SureshKBN
text:
The biggest scam in town is is calling PEAD/ EP a “strategy” based only on earnings notifications.

If it was that simple, algos would have arbitraged it away long back.

Real edge is in context, positioning, and capital flow  not notifications.

Context tells you where the company stands in its cycle:
Early rerating?
Peak margin?
Turnaround?
Structural compounding?

Positioning tells you who already owns the story.
Crowded trade ready to unwind?
Or under owned stock waiting for discovery?

Capital flow tells you what big money is doing after results.
Are dips getting bought?
Are supports defended?
Is size being built quietly?

author: SureshKBN
text:
Finolex Cables #HarResultKuchKehtaHai
#FANTASTIC

The headline numbers look exceptionally strong, but the real story is the structural margin transformation in the Communication Cables segment. Operating margins for this business skyrocketed to 29.8% this quarter, up from a mere 1.2% in the same period last year. This massive expansion is the direct result of the ₹100 Crore glass preform facility commissioned in March 2026. By backward-integrating, the company has insulated itself from global fiber supply bottlenecks and captured a highly profitable slice of the value chain.

Meanwhile, the core Electrical Cables segment demonstrated solid pricing power, growing 46.6% YoY to ₹1,767.45 Crore. Volume growth was a steady 7% YoY, supported by agricultural, industrial, and solar applications. This growth was achieved despite elevated copper prices, which the company successfully passed on through timely price hikes implemented in May. The low-margin Copper Rod plant was completely shut down due to Middle East war fuel shortages, but this had a negligible impact on overall profitability.

The balance sheet remains a fortress with zero net debt, ₹19.14 Crore of total borrowings, and a massive investment book of ₹4,337.24 Crore. While historical cash conversion was weak due to a strategic ₹300 Crore inventory pre-buy to hedge shipping risks, this high-cost inventory is now being liquidated into a high-demand environment, which should normalize cash flows. The stock trades at about 21 times earnings, while the company is on track to double its fiber draw capacity to 8 million fiber kilometers by Q3 FY2027, positioning it to capture massive demand from data centers and rural telecom connectivity.

author: SureshKBN
text:
Agree with your point , but especially in this kind of market phase, it’s important to look at the bear case with clarity:

US tariffs: The key question is how long they continue. If this goes beyond March, customers will naturally shift to other countries, or the company will have to absorb the margin hit.

US CV cycle: This remains a major driver. My working assumption is that the cycle should revive in the next 6 months.

Debt: It’s high. Not an immediate problem today, but it can’t be ignored while modelling risk.

Whether we agree with the market or not is secondary. It’s always useful to understand why the market is pricing something the way it is today. When real triggers finally show up, this preparation helps us react quickly and confidently.

Honestly, this process has helped me a lot. Even on the most inactive days, I make it a point to read at least 3–5 companies  where price action looks interesting  past, present, and future of fundamentals. This repeated exercise, and maintaining a clean watchlist, makes the actual decision making effortless when the opportunity comes.

contextText:
Sectoral Check

Just penned down a set of brief thoughts on some of the major themes to see where we stand. Do share your opinions!

(By one of our students who's brilliant at checking themes and stock @deveshkedia_ )

Disclaimer: not a buy or sell recommendation.

1. Bank & Financials - Out of favour at the moment. Asset quality still very good buy peak soon. Slow deposit growth restricting advances growth.

2. Wealth management & Brokers - Uncertainty looms on the broking side due to hike in charges & taxes on FnO. Wealth Mgmt. doing well across the board. Private equity becoming attractive by taxes coming down at par with public equity - this theme should also be a multi-year theme in play

3. Chemical & Fertilizers - Select names bottoming out but most of the names still struggling with oversupply and exports. Fertilizer companies doing well

4. IT - Growth has come in single digits but the worst seems to be behind them. Incremental flows clearly flowing towards the theme as the sector is coming out of a long corrective phase and is entering stage 2. Services companies doing decent but product companies are doing much better. ER&D companies also doing well.

5. Railways & Defence - Order inflows have been slow in Q1, with capex numbers still strong but almost flat compared to last year. Next few quarters should be good but not sure if they will be able to attract a big chunk of the incremental flows

6. Infrastructure - Some select names still offer value and the next few quarters should be good for them with better order inflow and execution. Theme continues to be in stage 2 but one has to be extremely selective here

7. Real Estate - Strong tailwinds and growth triggers in place. Sector coming in favour after a long decadal lull period. Selective premium realty names still offer value with a healthy pipeline of projects. Home financiers and proxies such as construction equipment and materials should also do well.

8. Power - Massive capex and targets announced by the government here. DISCOM health has improved signifivantly so power players overall should do well. Solar getting a big push while wind has been deprioritized. Proxies such as transformers, smart meters, EV charging, battery storage, cables and wires, etc. can be a good play here.

9. Travel & Hospitality - Q1 would've been weak but performance has picked up from Q2. Multi-year theme with tailwinds as the foreign inbound travel picks up further. Domestic & international outbound travel is doing very well. Supply Demand mismatch may continue to provide pricing power to the players.

10. Telecom - Another forgotten sector which is coming back in favour after a decade. Debt levels falling, consolidation of players and increasing tariffs is helping in increased profitability and health of the players. Equipement players benefitting with government push and exports picking up.

11. Textiles - Sector coming out of tailwinds offering decent risk reward if the growth picks up again. Whole theme has re-entered stage 2 with companies guiding for better capacity utilization and tapering Red Sea crisis issues.

12. Metals & Mining - Metal players may struggle due to chinese imports and volatile metal prices but the mining companies and proxies should do well. Mining has become a priority theme for the government and select players are expected to gain massively over the coming years with huge capex plans and healthy balance sheets

13. Auto & Auto Ancillaries - The sector continues to do well in stage 2. New launches and decent demand growth coming in. Ancillaries doing better with 2W demand growing strongly. Exports remain an interesting opportunity for a few players.

14. Pharma - Select pharma players doing very well with a healthy pipeline and growth visibility. M&A activities also picking up. Supply chains shifting from China may help further. Companies are extremely optimistic about the opportunities. Sector is in a strong stage 2.

15. Hospitals & Healthcare - Hospitals struggling to post strong numbers. Growth has been slow with some struggling with greenfield capex, and others unable to improve utilization levels. Diagnostic companies are showing goood improvement but are yet to surpass the covid-levels.

16. Ecommerce - Growth has been really fast with pricing power coming in play - which should result in improved profitability. Swiggy about to get listed soon, which should make it more interesting

17. Luxury - This is a multi-year theme in play. Watches, clothes, aviation, jewellery, malls, real estate etc. - all doing very well and are expected to continue the growth momentum

18. Water Infra & Pipes - The whole segment (Pipes, Pumps, Mgmt., etc.) is doing extremely well with strong focus by the government as well. New technologies such as OPVC also coming up. Growth has been very strong with improving margins and order books. Multi-year theme but execution should be tracked closely.

19. Recycling - Another multi-year theme doing well. Execution has been solid till now and the visibility is very strong. Domestic scrap availability is expected to increase in the coming years, lowering the WC days and improving margins.

20. FMCG - Another legacy sector coming back in focus due to rural consumption expected to do well. Growth has been in single digits but the sector remains a defensive flow attracting theme, doing well in stage 2.

text:
There are many pharma companies like this.

I’m not the kind of investor who puts 1% first, prays for events to happen, then adds another 2% after everything becomes obvious.

I try to study as many odds as possible before the price action accelerates.

Morepen was mainly a PEAD setup for me. I had been tracking it since the CDMO order, but the execution genuinely surprised me. Once earnings confirmed the fundamental pivot, I went with full force.

Whatever your style, preparation has to come first. Track the business, understand what can change the earnings trajectory, and wait patiently for that fundamental pivot.

When earnings finally confirm what you were waiting for, that is when you should be ready to pull the trigger with conviction.

I’m not the “hold for 10 years and find a 200-bagger” kind of investor.

I’d rather capture a much shorter, high-conviction earnings + price-action cycle with meaningful allocation and make a bigger impact on the portfolio with great position sizing .

author: SureshKBN
text:
I was here from 2010.

Life was cool when I was not known, or when I had less than 500 followers.

I started posting more after quitting my job three years back, and even more after my knee ACL surgery.

I did every mistake a new investor does.

You name it, I might have done it.

Bought stocks from Moneycontrol discussion boards 20 years ago without understanding the business or risks.

After some initial success, got false confidence, took a ₹2 lakh personal loan, invested it, and burned almost everything.

Averaged down thinking price has to come back.

Bought penny stocks and low market-cap names thinking they will rise fast.

Followed TV recommendations.

Every stupid mistake a beginner investor makes, I have done it.

In Telugu there is a line:

“Bhogi kaanivaadu Yogi kaaledu.”

One who has not gone through indulgence, mistakes, burns and temptations cannot become wise like a yogi.

So when I say something today, it is not theory.

It is burn marks speaking.

--------
Other mistakes I did as a new investor:

Buying just because the stock had fallen 50%, thinking it had become cheap.

Confusing low price with cheap valuation  ₹10 stock looked cheaper than ₹1,000 stock.

Looking only at profits, not cash flow, debt, pledging, dilution or promoter quality.

Selling winners too early and holding losers forever.

Thinking every operator-driven move is “smart money accumulation.”

Believing every turnaround story without checking whether the balance sheet can survive.

Buying because some big investor entered, without understanding their time horizon or position size.

Taking allocation too big in stocks I did not understand properly.

Not respecting liquidity — easy to enter, impossible to exit.

Getting emotionally attached to stocks and defending them like family members.

Mistaking bull market luck for personal skill.

Thinking more information means better decision-making.

Watching price every day but not watching business progress.

Ignoring opportunity cost  holding dead stocks while better stocks kept moving.

Learning risk only after losing money.

author: SureshKBN
text:
After PEAD ,

 I check just ONE simple thing:Did the stock start moving before the results?

Meaning: was smart money already buying and “expecting” good numbers?

If YES (it moved before):
Expectations were already built → good results may be “priced in” → I wait.

Let the excitement cool down, weak hands exit, price settles… then decide.

If NO (it didn’t move before):
Results were a real surprise → re-rating starts after the print → I act early.

This is why some moves continue:
Bajaj Consumer ~35% up, STL Tech ~50% up.PEAD works best when expectations were low.

author: SureshKBN
text: act as my real-time corporate-action scanner for all NSE & BSE-listed companies.  Data window: Look at disclosures, exchange filings (BSE & NSE), SEBI announcements, press releases, investor presentations, earnings-call transcripts, and top-tier business media published in the last 24 hours.  Filter for price-sensitive triggers that historically lead to re-rating or sharp moves (≥ ±5 %). Include only events such as: • Large order/contract wins (≥ ₹100 crore or ≥ 0.5 × FY25 revenue) • Capacity expansions, green-field projects, or large capex approvals (≥ ₹100 crore) • Regulatory approvals / license wins (FDA, DGCA, environment, mining, spectrum, etc.) • M&A, stake sales, delisting, buy-backs, bonus/stock-split proposals, or big promoter/insider trades • Guidance upgrades/downgrades, margin/volume surprises in results, or material ESG controversies • Index inclusion/exclusion (Nifty family, MSCI, FTSE) or F&O ban-list changes  Output: Give a concise table sorted by likely impact (High ▸ Medium ▸ Low). Columns: | Company | Ticker | Catalyst (≤ 10 words) | Quick Take (≤ 25 words on why it matters) | Impact (High/Med/Low) | Source |  Brevity: Limit the entire brief to ≤ 12 rows and ≤ 300 words.  Analyst tone: Neutral, fact-led, no hype. End with a one-line “Use-case hint” (e.g., “Set an alert if volume spikes above 3 × 30-day avg”).  Citations: After each row, cite the source(s) using numbered footnotes or inline IDs.  Skip routine dividend or AGM notices unless they coincide with a special payout or strategic reveal.

📻The MISERABLE🥲 State of India's Battery Energy Storage (BESS) Manufacturing!   VIRTUALLY ZERO, after the big fanfare launch of PLI Scheme in 2022.  Incidentally, the best progress is by Exide and Amara Raja who didn't win incentive under PLI

🟢Who are the potential  players & what is the status? From Grok:

The status of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) manufacturing  by Reliance, Ola Electric, Rajesh Exports,   Exide Industries,  Amara Raja & GP Eco Solar

Reliance Industries (Failed to Manufacture, so far)

Reliance New Energy Ltd. (RNEL), a subsidiary of Reliance Industries, has faced challenges in its battery manufacturing ambitions under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme. It secured incentives for 5 GWh in 2022 and an additional 10 GWh in 2024, targeting a total of 15 GWh of advanced chemistry cell (ACC) capacity. However, as of early 2025, Reliance has been penalized for delays. The Ministry of Heavy Industries imposed liquidated damages (LD) of Rs 3.1 crore by March 3, 2025, for missing Milestone 1 (25% domestic value addition within two years) for its initial 5 GWh commitment. Reliance sought an extension, citing global market uncertainties and high capital costs, with its Jamnagar Gigafactory not yet operational.

Ola Electric Mobility - Only EV batteries

Ola Electric, awarded 20 GWh under the PLI scheme in 2022, has made some progress. Its gigafactory in Tamil Nadu began trial production of lithium-ion cells (4680 form factor) in March 2024, with an initial capacity of 1 GWh, expandable to 20 GWh. Ola claims commercial production started by early 2025, focusing on cells for its electric vehicles (EVs). However, there’s no specific evidence tying these cells to utility-scale BESS projects. Ola’s focus has been EV batteries,

Rajesh Exports (Potential Scam)

Rajesh Exports, a jewelry firm diversifying into batteries, won 5 GWh under the PLI scheme in 2022, with plans for a facility in Karnataka.

However, progress is murky. By March 2025, it faced scrutiny for missing deadlines, alongside Reliance and Ola, though no specific penalty has been publicized for it yet. Critics, including sentiments on X, label it a potential “scam” to secure government incentives, given its lack of expertise in battery tech and no visible manufacturing output. There’s no concrete proof of Rajesh Exports producing BESS batteries—or any batteries—domestically. Its stock rose 5.9% in July 2022 after the PLI win, but operational silence since then fuels skepticism. It’s plausible they’ve produced nothing tangible, relying on intent rather than execution.

Exide Industries and Amara Raja

Exide Industries and Amara Raja, traditional lead-acid battery makers, are transitioning to lithium-ion for energy storage. Exide invested Rs 149.99 crore in its subsidiary Exide Energy Solutions by 2024, aiming for a lithium-ion plant, but no commissioning has occurred by March 2025.

Amara Raja broke ground on a gigafactory in Telangana in 2023, targeting 16 GWh by 2030, with the first phase (1-2 GWh) expected in 2025-2026. Neither has operational BESS battery production yet. Both are scaling up, but their plants remain under construction or in planning, meaning no domestic output exists as of now.

GP Eco Solutions: (New kid in the game)

GP Eco Solutions is investing in a 4.5 GWh BESS capacity increase through the Uttar Pradesh Gigafactory, bringing its total to 5 GWh by Q3 FY 2025-26.    However, whether this involves manufacturing BESS cells domestically or assembling imported ones remains unclear—current evidence leans toward assembly. This strengthens GP Eco’s potential as a BESS player, but it’s not yet a confirmed cell manufacturer like Exide or Amara Raja aim to be.

Are 100% of BESS Batteries Imported, Currently?

As of March 2025, India’s installed BESS capacity is 219.1 MWh (111.7 MW), per the BusinessLine article from March 2024, with 120 MWh added in Q1 2024. The key question is whether all batteries for these systems are imported?  Evidence suggests a heavy reliance on imports:

Lithium-ion cells, the backbone of BESS, are predominantly sourced from China, South Korea, and Japan (e.g., Panasonic, LG Chem, Samsung SDI).

For BESS specifically, lacking a robust domestic supply chain, the figure likely nears 100% for the cells themselves.

The truth is that India’s BESS battery manufacturing is embryonic. While some domestic assembly exists, the critical cells are overwhelmingly imported. Until PLI projects fully materialize—likely post-2026—India remains dependent on foreign supply chains for BESS batteries, making  “100% imported” claim functionally accurate for now.

contextText:
Impact of Interest Rates on Financial Companies in India (2010-2025)

How Interest Rates Affect Financial Companies

Interesting results by @AskPerplexity
@SureshKBN

⭐️The RBI repo rate chart from 2010-2025 shows several distinct phases:

-2010-2012: Sharp increase from 5.25% to 8%

-2012-2014: High but fluctuating rates (7.25-8%)

-2014-2019: Gradual decline to 5.15%

-2019-2021: Steep cut to 4% (COVID response)

-2021-2024: Rapid increase to 6.5%

- 2025: Slight moderation to 6.25%

⭐️Impact on Different Financial Segments

1. Banks

When rates fall: Net interest margins (NIMs) typically compress, but loan volumes increase

When rates rise: NIMs expand as loan yields increase faster than deposit costs

Performance trends: Private banks like HDFC Bank, Kotak, and ICICI showed stronger profitability during the 2019-2021 low-rate period due to high CASA ratios, while public sector banks struggled with NPAs regardless of the rate environment

2. NBFCs

When rates fall: Benefit from lower borrowing costs and increased loan demand

When rates rise: Face margin pressure as their cost of funds increases faster than their ability to raise lending rates

Performance trends: NBFCs like Bajaj Finance thrived during 2014-2019 as rates gradually declined, but faced challenges during 2010-2012 (rising rates) and post-2022 (rapid rate hikes)

3. Housing Finance Companies

When rates fall: Housing loan demand surges due to improved affordability

Performance trends: Companies like HDFC Ltd (pre-merger) showed strong growth during 2018-2021 when rates were declining/low

4. Small Finance Banks & Microfinance

Rate sensitivity: Less affected by rate changes as their lending rates are higher and based on operational costs

Performance trends: Maintained stable NIMs across rate cycles

5. Insurance Companies

When rates fall: Life insurers struggle to generate returns to match guaranteed policies

Performance trends: Life insurers like LIC performed better in higher rate environments (2010-2014)

6. Asset Management Companies

When rates fall: Bond funds see valuation gains; equity funds benefit from market rallies

Performance trends: AMCs like HDFC AMC saw AUM growth during the 2018-2021 rate decline phase

⭐️Conclusion: Financial Segments Most Likely to Benefit from Rate Reductions

Based on historical performance during different interest rate cycles (2010-2025), these sectors would benefit most from interest rate reductions:

- Housing Finance Companies:

Lower rates directly improve housing affordability, boosting loan demand

Companies like LIC Housing Finance and PNB Housing Finance would see immediate NP growth

- Retail-Focused NBFCs:

Consumer lenders like Bajaj Finance and Shriram Finance benefit from lower borrowing costs

Their high-margin retail portfolios allow them to maintain lending rates while reducing funding costs

-Private Banks with High CASA Ratios:

Banks with strong low-cost deposit bases like HDFC Bank and Kotak maintain margins even during rate cuts
Benefit from increased credit demand while minimizing deposit cost increases

Gold Loan NBFCs:

Companies like Muthoot Finance and Manappuram maintain high lending rates despite rate cuts
Benefit from lower borrowing costs, directly improving net profit margins

Asset Management Companies:

AMCs benefit from valuation gains in bond portfolios and increased investor flows from fixed deposits to mutual funds

Rate cuts typically boost both debt and equity AUM, driving fee income

The most dramatic profit improvements would likely be seen in housing finance and retail NBFCs, where rate cuts directly drive both margin expansion and volume growth.

SK Hynix is expected to deliver all time high ROE in 2026, while Samsung Electronics ROE is also rising meaningfully

Asia-Pacific ROE is projected to move from ~10% in 2023 to ~15% by 2027, led by semiconductor & AI hardware suppliers

Value is migrating from AI platform owners to “picks & shovels” suppliers

author: SureshKBN
text:
As I said  no one got this :)

Real earnings = What the company actually reports.
 Perception of earnings = What the market believes future earnings will be.
Markets price future perception, not current numbers.

If perception improves → stock rerates.
If perception weakens → stock derates.
Even if real earnings are good r bad .

👉 The gap between perception and reality = opportunity.

The real issue is this  I’ve contradicted myself multiple times depending on market context.
You can spot it easily if you go through my tweets:

Earlier, I used to scan for stocks hitting 52-week highs or near highs - typical bull market euphoria.

Then came a phase of tracking top gainers of the day.

And now, it’s all about Q4 turnarounds.

What I didn’t consciously realize was that my recent entries had a clear pattern -  Q4 turnarounds, different risk appetite, PF sizing, and entry prices. That makes a huge difference.

My concern is simple: if I casually say something and someone applies it in a different market context, it could be a disaster.

Everything I do is centered on one thing — how to maximize gains.
The rest? Just reverse engineering, trial and error… and finding what works.

author: SureshKBN
text:
During a bear market, you often get a "shakeout" in some form on the right side of a base during the bottoming process. The "reason" is usually attributed to some scary news item that fuels negative sentiment and leans on investors that have already been beaten up and worn out emotionally as well as financially. This leads to the final selling and marks the shift from weak hands to strong hands, creating the conditions necessary for a new uptrend. Debt ceiling issues, inflation worries, recession speculation and Fed language are all plausible scapegoats.

But as we look back at history and as I reflect on the nine bear markets I have lived through personally, it was always during these "scary" times that bottoms were formed and a great opportunity was about to be born.

The question is, going forward... what part of the historic narrative are you going to choose to be part of? Will you be a victim of your own idiosyncrasies and blame the market and the system/ Will you throw in the towel at the wrong time and flush all your hard work down the toilet due to impatience? Or will you be among the rare participants that remain disciplined, sticks to the rules, and as a result, defy the odds?

The way I cut through the noise and navigate these tumultuous times ensuring that I do not fall victim to my own emotions, is not by having a crystal ball or even through my experience and skill. It's by focusing on the individual stocks and sticking to sound buying and selling principles. It's through having and trusting rules.

In 40-years, my rules-based bottoms up or "stocks have the final say" approach has not let me down. My opinion and my emotions take a back seat to verdict of the market. I expose my capital to the best and plan for the worst. i only get aggressive when my trades are working, and I always cut back and trade small when they are not. In doing so, I create asymmetric leverage and beat the market time and time again. Meanwhile, the undisciplined, the skeptics and the quitters spectate in disbelief and wonder... how did he do it? He must have gotten lucky!

My response. After four decades, trading through nine bull markets and nine bear markets (including four of the worst bear markets and crashes in stock market history) and hundreds of thousands of stock trades, I would guess that I would have to be the luckiest guy in the world.

Or maybe (just a thought) discipline, strategy, hard work and commitment actually pays off, and the market is not completely random? Maybe this craft of stock trading is not just a hobby or a sport (at least for some of us). Maybe trading and investing is actually a business. And like any other business, there are principles that allow for a successful enterprise.

I can assure you it's the later, and I can also assure you that you have the potential to match and even exceed my own success. The future will be filled with opportunity. But I can also assure that you will have to dig deep and muster up the courage to think and act like a champion. Because greatness is not handed out like candy on Halloween. To the contrary, it's reserved for those that deserve it, and your worthiness will be tested over and over again.

Knowledge and opportunity does not automatically lead to success; it's what you do with the knowledge and how you handle opportunity when it comes knocking.

Step one: Stop worrying. Stop complaining. Stop making excuses. Stop believing the clowns that never experienced huge success. Follow and emulate proven individuals and proven methods. Put your head down and do the work. Be patient. Remain disciplined and your future will be bright enough to light the way for those who choose to travel in your footsteps.

contextText:
“India Data Centers – 5x in 5 years”

The instinct is to get excited.

But what lies beneath the headline?

The first-order story is clear: explosive data growth, AI adoption, digital payments, OTT streaming, and regulatory push for data localization. That’s what everyone sees.

Do you see the second and third-order effects?

Questions that separate narrative from reality:

1. Demand vs. Hype

-How much of the projected demand is hyperscaler cloud vs. BFSI vs. AI training?

-What portion is truly India-locked due to regulation/latency, and what can shift offshore?

-How much is committed (pre-leased contracts) vs. just assumptions in a model?

-If AI racks consume 5–6× more power, are forecasts assuming more racks or just denser racks?

2. Supply Bottlenecks

-Where is the actual constraint: land, power, permits, cooling, or substation capacity?

-How much capacity is energized today vs. still a “paper pipeline”?

-Are Mumbai/Chennai landing station adjacencies already spoken for, forcing spillover into Tier-2 hubs?

3. Value Capture

-Who captures economics: telcos (Airtel Nxtra, Jio), infra JVs (AdaniConneX), or global players (NTT, Equinix)?

-Is this an oligopoly with pricing power, or a capacity arms race that leads to compression?

-Where’s the moat: land + power, interconnect richness, SLA reliability, or renewable PPAs?

4. Pricing & Contracts

-What’s the real Rs/kW-month after incentives and free rent?

-Are contracts 5–10 years take-or-pay with escalators, or shorter and repriced?

-How sensitive are margins to a 15–20% price drop if supply overshoots?

5. Unit Economics

-What’s the yield-on-cost after accounting for land, shell, power infra, cooling, and fit-outs?

-What occupancy is needed to cover the cost of capital?

-How resilient are returns if power tariffs spike, or projects are delayed by 6–12 months?

6. Power is the Real Governor

-Can DISCOMs and substations actually handle 100–200 MW step-ups?

-Are there 24×7 renewable PPAs, or will operators face grid volatility and ESG pushback?

-What happens when data centers compete with EVs and industry for scarce megawatts?

7. Technology & Obsolescence

-Are facilities future-ready for 50–100 kW racks with liquid cooling?

-Could today’s designs get stranded if workloads shift to edge or immersion setups?

8. Already in the Price?

-Reverse-DCF: what occupancy, pricing, and timelines are baked into current valuations?

-Are investors paying for a full pipeline delivery that historically converts only 30–40% on time?

-How do EV/MW and EV/EBITDA multiples stack up vs. global peers, after adjusting for Indian risks?

The lesson: When brokerages paint a 5× growth picture, don’t just ask “Is this true?”.

Ask: “Even if it is, who captures the value? At what cost? And how much is already priced in?”

The best investors don’t stop at the headline—they chase the second- and third-order consequences.

#DataCenters #InvestingInsights #DigitalInfrastructure #IndiaGrowthStory #SecondOrderThinking

author: SureshKBN
text:
1. Smart Money Accumulates Quietly
When institutions want to build a position, they do it gradually to avoid driving up prices too quickly.
This accumulation phase often happens when the stock is out of favor, underperforming, or in a consolidation range.
You’ll see relatively low trading volumes with periodic spikes.
2. Stock Rallies & Retail Interest Grows
As the stock starts moving up, media coverage, social media hype, and positive earnings reports attract retail investors.
By this time, institutions have already built a solid position.
Price action looks strong, and more people jump in, thinking the rally has just begun.
3. Smart Money Distributes Holdings
Once retail participation increases, institutions begin offloading their positions.
This distribution happens gradually so that it doesn’t trigger panic selling.
You might see high volume on up days, but the stock struggles to make new highs.
4. Price Rolls Over, Leaving Retail Holding the Bag
After exiting, the stock suddenly faces selling pressure.
Without institutional support, it struggles to sustain higher prices.
Retail traders, seeing losses, either panic sell or hold on, hoping for a recovery that may never come.
How to Avoid This Trap?
Look at Volume Trends: If a stock has been rising with declining volume, it might indicate a distribution phase.
Track Institutional Activity: Bulk/block deals, FII/DII holdings, and insider selling are red flags.
Watch for Failed Breakouts: If a stock repeatedly fails to sustain new highs, smart money could be exiting.
Post-Earnings Moves: If a stock reacts poorly despite good results, institutions might be selling into strength.

author: SureshKBN
text:
Carysil's leadership, particularly under Chirag Parekh (CMD), appears to be strategic and execution-focused. Here’s how I’d assess them across key parameters:

Strengths
✅ Strategic Vision – They have a clear roadmap, expanding into high-margin products (workstation sinks, built-in appliances, faucets) and focusing on premium positioning.
✅ Global Expansion – Strong execution in international markets, with partnerships like IKEA & Karran, positioning themselves well in the Quartz sink market.
✅ Operational Efficiency – Investments in automation, capacity utilization improvement (65% → 80%), and cost optimization (freight, raw materials).
✅ Adaptability – Despite demand slowdowns, they pivot towards value-driven growth (high-margin products) instead of chasing volume.
Weaknesses & Risks
⚠️ US Business Struggles – Their United Surfaces subsidiary has faced losses and is still in a turnaround phase. Expansion in the US has been slower than expected, considering the market size.
⚠️ Execution Delays – While they talk about strong order flows (Karran, IKEA, Kohler), realization takes time, and past targets (₹1,000 crore revenue) have been pushed forward.
⚠️ Marketing & Brand Building in India – The Sternhagen brand (luxury bathroom solutions) hasn’t scaled well, and while they’re spending on marketing (~8-10% of sales), domestic growth has been muted.
⚠️ Working Capital Management – High inventory levels in some segments, delays in order execution, and ₹255 crore debt remain areas to watch.
Overall Rating (On a Scale of 10)

🔹 Strategic Vision & Growth Execution – 8/10
🔹 Financial & Operational Management – 7/10 (Margins & working capital still need improvement)
🔹 Global Expansion & Partnerships – 8.5/10
🔹 India Business & Branding Efforts – 6.5/10
🔹 Transparency & Investor Communication – 8/10 (Detailed concalls, but some execution delays)
Final Verdict
Carysil's leadership is strong in strategy and expansion but needs to improve execution timelines. If they can turn around US operations, scale premium India offerings, and stabilize margins, the company could break the ₹1,000 crore revenue & ₹100 crore PAT mark soon.
